 The Hon'Ble Smt. Justice M.G. Priyadarsini
 M.A.C.M.A.No. 596 of 2017
Judgment:

This appeal is preferred by IFFCO-TOKIO General Insurance Company Limited, questioning the order and decree, dated 13.01.2016 passed in O.P.No. 299 of 2011 on the file of the Chairman, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-cum-XIII Additional Chief Judge (Fast Track Court), City Civil Court,
Hyderabad (for short, the Tribunal).
2.

entities.text:
Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-cum-XIII Additional Chief Judge (Fast Track Court), City Civil Court,
Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: For the sake of convenience, the parties have been referred to as arrayed before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are that the claimant-injured being minor, was represented by her father,
filed a petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by her in a road accident that occurred on 22.01.2008.

It is stated that on the fateful day, at about 08:30 a.m., when the claimant was attending her nature calls, one Tractor bearing No.AP 22 N 744 attached with trailer (water tanker) bearing No.AP 22 T 4256 owned by respondent No.1, insured with respondent No. 2, being driven by its driver, came in a rash and negligent manner MGP, J Macma_596_2017 at high speed from reverse direction.
As a result, the driver of the crime vehicle lost control of the vehicle and the tractor and trailer fell on the left leg of the claimant.
Due to the said impact, the claimant received fracture to left leg and other bleeding injuries all over the body.
Immediately, she was shifted to Government Hospital, Vikarabad and thereafter shifted to Yashoda Multi Speciality Hospital, Malakpet, for better treatment.
She spent huge amounts towards medical and incidental charges.
Due to the said accident, she sustained permanent disability and lost her academic year.
Therefore, she laid the claim against the respondents seeking compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- under various heads.

4. Before the Tribunal, while respondent No. 1 remained ex parte, respondent No. 2 filed counter denying the averments made in the claim petition, the age, occupation, injuries, treatment and disability of the claimant.
He further contended that the compensation claimed by the claimant is highly excessive and exorbitant and prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. Considering the claim and the counter filed by respondent No. 2 and on evaluation of the evidence, both oral and documentary, the Tribunal has allowed the O.P. and awarded MGP, J Macma_596_2017 compensation of Rs.13,80,000/- with interest at 9% per annum.
Challenging the same, the present appeal has been filed by the Insurance Company.

6. Heard both sides and perused the record.

sentences.text: The main contention of the learned Standing Counsel for the Insurance Company is that the driver of the offending vehicle was not having valid driving licence at the time of the accident.

Insofar as the quantum of compensation, the learned Standing Counsel has contended that though the claimant filed medical bills for Rs.41,753/-and Rs.54,758/-, the Tribunal erred in granting Rs.2,00,000/- towards present, past and future medical expenses.

It is further submitted that the Tribunal awarded excess amounts of Rs.2,00,000/- for extra nourishment, travelling and attendant charges, Rs.3,00,000/- for the loss of marriage prospects and other amenities.
It is further contended that the Tribunal has already granted Rs.1,80,000/- for the disability sustained by the claimant, however erred in awarding Rs.3,00,000/- towards loss of earnings.

The learned Standing Counsel further contended that the interest granted by the Tribunal @ 9% is excessive and as MGP,
J Macma_596_2017 held by the Apex Court in several decisions interest should be granted @ 7.5%.
8.

The learned counsel for the claimant, per contra, supported the award and decree passed by the Tribunal and also fastening the liability on the Insurance Company to pay the compensation and contended that the learned Tribunal has rightly awarded compensation and the same needs no interference.

9. A perusal of the impugned order discloses that the Tribunal has framed issue No.1 as to whether the accident took place due to the rash and negligent driving of the vehicle tractor bearing No. AP 22 N 744 and trailer bearing No. AP 22 T 4256 causing injuries to the claimant, and after considering the evidence of P.W.1 coupled with the documentary evidence i.e., Ex.A1, First Information Report;
Ex.A2, Charge Sheet, the tribunal has categorically observed that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the crime vehicle i.e., Tractor bearing No. AP 22 N 744 coupled with trailer bearing No. AP 22 T 4256 by its driver and has answered the issue in favour of the claimant and against the respondents.
Therefore, I see no reason to interfere with the finding of the MGP, J Macma_596_2017 Tribunal that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the Crime vehicle by its driver.

10. As regards the contention of the learned Standing Counsel for the appellant that the Tribunal erred in fastening the liability on the insurance company only on the aspect that the driver of the offending vehicle was not having valid driving licence at the time of the accident and that except the oral evidence of RW.1, no evidence in that regard was let in before the Tribunal.

This Court has perused the evidence let in by the Insurance Company where in it discloses that except the plea that the driver of the Offending Vehicle has no driving licence, the Insurance Company/appellant has not adduced any evidence such as examining the officials of RTO.
Therefore, the contention of learned standing Counsel for the Insurance Company is unsustainable.

11. As regards the quantum of compensation, a perusal of the medical evidence of PW. 2, Orthopedic Surgeon at Yashoda Hospital and PW. 4, Civil Surgeon, Coupled with Ex.A.7, disability certificate issued by District Medical Board, Vikarabad medical camp, Ranga Reddy District, reveals that the claimant has sustained 60% permanent disability due to amputation of MGP, J Macma_596_2017 left leg above knee.

A perusal of the impugned order discloses that the Tribunal has awarded Rs.1,80,000/- for the disability sustained by the claimant; Rs.2,00,000/- towards present, past and future medical expenses; Rs.1,00,000/- towards pain and suffering; Rs.2,00,000/- for extra Iffcotokio Gen. Ins. Com. Ltd., ... vs B. Nikitha, Hyderabad And 1 Other on 15 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58571652/
2 nourishment, travelling and attendant charges; Rs.1,00,000/- for the physiotherapy and artificial limb and Rs.3,00,000/- for the loss of future amenities i.e., marriage prospects etc., as the claimant,
who is aged about 8 years girl sustained 60% permanent disability in view of amputation of her left leg.

Though the Tribunal has adequately granted those amounts, in fact on higher side, this Court is not inclined to interfere with the same, however, awarding Rs.3,00,000/- under the head of loss of earnings and future loss of studies is unsustainable for the reason that the claimant is 8 years old girl, studying.
Hence, loss of earnings does not arise as she is not earning anything.
Further, the claimant can continue her studies as there will not be any obstruction for her to continue her studies by attending the school, by using artificial limb and further taking physiotherapy.
Further, the amounts on all heads are adequately awarded including artificial limb and physiotherapy.

Hence,
this Court is declined MGP, J Macma_596_2017 to accept the aforesaid sum.

Thus, the compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal is reduced from Rs.13,80,000/- to Rs.10,80,000/-.
12.

Insofar as the interest awarded by the Tribunal is concerned, as rightly pointed out by the learned Standing Counsel for the Insurance Company that as per the decision of the Apex Court in Rajesh and others v. Rajbir Singh and others1 the rate of interest is hereby reduced from 9% to 7.5%
per annum on the compensation awarded by the Tribunal from the date of petition till the date of realization.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 13. Accordingly, the M.A.C.M.A is partly allowed reducing the compensation amount from Rs.13,80,000/- to Rs.10,80,000/- together with interest at 7.5% per annum from the date of petition till date of realization.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending shall stand closed.
JUSTICE M.G. PRIYADARSINI 15.06.2023 gms 1 2013 ACJ 1403 = 2013 (4) ALT 35 MGP, J Macma_596_2017 THE HON'BLE SMT.
